[head=2][color=#684871]Divine Sol Mandate[/color][/head]
Forged from the wreck of the Solarian Ascendancy, the Divine Sol Mandate rallied under feudal ideals and conquered most of Known Space. Centuries of rebellion have since worn them down to a secondary power, but the Mandate remains proud, disciplined, and dangerous.
Imperial society runs on [bold]rank and blood[/bold]. Nobles command, knights serve with honor, and the common levy fights and dies for both. Formality is not optional here, since it is the glue that holds the whole order together.
[head=3][color=#684871]Nobility and Command[/color][/head]
- [bold]Lord Admiral.[/bold] Also called the Governor, this is the ruling authority and commander of Imperial forces in the region. - [bold]Imperial Adjutant.[/bold] The Lord Admiral's right hand and the executor of orders. - [bold]Courtier[/bold] and [bold]Minister of Finance.[/bold] The court and administration that run the war effort.
[head=3][color=#684871]Knights[/color][/head]
- [bold]Knight Banneret.[/bold] A senior knight who leads men into battle. - [bold]Knight Templar[/bold] and [bold]Advocatus.[/bold] Knights of the Imperial judiciary and faith.
[head=3][color=#684871]Levy and Support[/color][/head]
- [bold]Man-at-Arms.[/bold] Also called the Levyman, this is the professional core of the Imperial infantry. - [bold]Freeholder.[/bold] A common soldier of the levy and the newcomer's role. - [bold]Imperial Foreman[/bold] and [bold]Imperial Scribe.[/bold] They run labor, engineering, and records. - [bold]Imperial Surgeon.[/bold] The Mandate's field medic and physician.
[head=3][color=#684871]How to address them[/color][/head]
Speak [bold]formally[/bold] and always defer upward. Sloppy address insults a knight and can be a crime before a noble.
- A knight is addressed as [color=#684871][bold]Ser[/bold][/color], as in "As you command, Ser." - Officers and commanders are [color=#684871][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color]. - Nobles and high lords are [color=#684871][bold]My Lord[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]My Lady[/bold][/color], or addressed by their title, such as Governor or Lord Admiral.
See the [color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color] page for more.
